classes.name: Gyelyong Tshogdu general election
classes.locator: https://oag.gov.bt/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Constitution_of_Bhutan.pdf (Art. 12.1: a maximum of fifty-five members, each constituency directly electing one member; Art. 15.5-15.8: only the two parties placed first and second in the primary round contest the general election)
classes.note: First past the post in 47 single-member constituencies (demkhongs), at most 55 under Art. 12.1, with 2 to 7 per dzongkhag (Election Act 2008 s.5). Only the two parties placed first and second in the primary round stand; in 2008 only two parties registered, so no primary round was held. Results give EVM and postal votes by constituency. The party winning most seats forms the government and its leader is made Prime Minister (Art. 17.1).

cadence.locator: https://oag.gov.bt/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Constitution_of_Bhutan.pdf (Art. 10.24: the National Assembly continues for five years from its first sitting unless dissolved early; Art. 15.6: a primary round on the expiry of the term or on dissolution)
cadence.vacancy_rule: A vacancy is filled by a bye-election within ninety days, unless less than 180 days of the term remain (Constitution Art. 15.9; Election Act 2008 s.579).

access.license: No license stated; published by the Election Commission of Bhutan
access.evidence: Result tables by constituency for 2008, 2013, and 2018 with EVM and postal votes (NA-ResultsFinal-2008.pdf, result.pdf, Annexure-2.pdf); the 2024 general election has a page (national-assembly-election-2023-2024) whose files were not read from here

dates.note: First elections to the National Assembly; two parties, no primary round.

classes.name: Gyelyong Tshogdu primary round
classes.locator: https://oag.gov.bt/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Constitution_of_Bhutan.pdf (Art. 15.5-15.7: a primary round in which all registered parties may take part selects the two parties for the general election)
classes.note: A state-run party vote held by the Commission on the full electorate: every registered party is on the ballot in every constituency, and the two with the most votes nationally go on to the general election. The archive holds it as one national list contest with constituency units.

access.license: No license stated; published by the Election Commission of Bhutan

classes.name: Gyelyong Tshogde election
classes.locator: https://oag.gov.bt/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Constitution_of_Bhutan.pdf (Art. 11.1: one member elected by the voters in each of the twenty Dzongkhags and five eminent persons nominated by the Druk Gyalpo)
classes.note: First past the post, one member per dzongkhag; candidates may not belong to a party (Art. 11.3). Each gewog and dzongkhag thromde first picks one candidate at a zomdu (class nc_zomdu). The five eminent members are nominated by the Druk Gyalpo, not elected. In 2007-08 fifteen dzongkhags voted on 31 December 2007 and the other five in January 2008.

classes.name: Zomdu for National Council candidates
classes.locator: https://oag.gov.bt/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Election-Act-of-Bhutan-2008both-Dzongkha-English.pdf (s.11: every gewog and dzongkhag thromde nominates one National Council candidate at a zomdu by majority vote of the registered voters present, with a polling station set up by the Dzongkhag Electoral Officer)
classes.disposition_reason: The zomdu is a state-run nominating vote in each gewog and thromde, but the Commission publishes only the resulting candidate lists, not the zomdu tallies.

classes.name: National Referendum
classes.locator: https://oag.gov.bt/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Constitution_of_Bhutan.pdf (Art. 34: the Druk Gyalpo may command a National Referendum on a bill not passed in a joint sitting or on the appeal of half the members of all Dzongkhag Tshogdus; Art. 2.24-2.26 (abdication); Art. 35.3)
classes.note: Decided by a simple majority of votes cast (Art. 34.1), under the National Referendum Act 2008. None has been held.

classes.name: Lyonchhen
classes.locator: https://oag.gov.bt/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Constitution_of_Bhutan.pdf (Art. 17.1: the Druk Gyalpo confers Dakyen on the leader or nominee of the party that wins the majority of seats in the National Assembly)
classes.disposition_reason: No vote is held: the Druk Gyalpo appoints the leader or nominee of the majority party (Art. 17.1). The Druk Gyalpo is a hereditary monarch (Art. 2), so the head of state is never elected either.

classes.name: Drangpon
classes.locator: https://oag.gov.bt/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Constitution_of_Bhutan.pdf (Art. 21.4-21.5: the Chief Justice and Drangpons are appointed by the Druk Gyalpo in consultation with the National Judicial Commission)
classes.disposition_reason: Every judge is appointed by the Druk Gyalpo; no judicial office is elected.

classes.name: Party candidate selection
classes.disposition_reason: Parties pick their National Assembly candidates under their own rules; the state neither runs nor publishes the selections. The state-run step, the primary round, is class na_primary.

classes.name: Dzongkhag Tshogdu Chairperson
classes.locator: https://oag.gov.bt/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Constitution_of_Bhutan.pdf (Art. 22.11: the Dzongkhag Tshogdu elects a Chairperson from among its members)
classes.disposition_reason: Each Dzongkhag Tshogdu elects its chairperson from among its own members at its sitting; the Commission does not run or publish the vote.

classes.name: Dzongkhag Tshogdu Thromde Thuemi

classes.note: Elected at the Local Government Elections; the 2011 results have a separate Thromde Thuemi file. The Dzongkhag Tshogdu is otherwise made up of the Gups and Mangmis.

classes.note: Bye-elections for any Gup, Mangmi, Tshogpa, Thrompon, or Thuemi seat, within thirty days of the vacancy. The Commission posts each declaration (for example Garzhikha_Omchheygang and Zamding chiwogs in Wangdue Phodrang, and Dhangkhar_Trong chiwog in Zhemgang).

cadence.locator: https://oag.gov.bt/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Election-Act-of-Bhutan-2008both-Dzongkha-English.pdf (s.579: Local Government bye-elections within thirty days of the vacancy)

access.license: No license stated; published by the Election Commission of Bhutan
access.evidence: Declarations of results for each Local Government bye-election, as web posts

dates.note: No official list of Local Government bye-elections has been compiled yet.

classes.name: Tshogdu
classes.locator: Introduction, p. xix (the National Assembly (Gyelyong Tshogdu))
classes.note: Before the Constitution the Tshogdu held chimis chosen by the people of each gewog (one vote per household), alongside representatives of the monastic body and government nominees. It ended when the elected National Assembly first sat in 2008.
classes.disposition_reason: No official source publishes the chimi selections; the National Assembly's own site (nab.gov.bt) does not answer from here and the Commission's records begin in 2007.

classes.name: Gup, Mangmi, and Tshogpa before 2011
classes.name_en: Gups and gewog bodies before the Local Government Act 2009
classes.locator: Introduction, p. xix: "Dzongkhag Tshogdu was established in 1981 ... the Gewog Tshogde was established in 1991"
classes.note: Gups, Mangmis, and Tshogpas of the Dzongkhag Yargay Tshogdu and Gewog Yargay Tshogchhung chosen under royal decrees and chathrims before the Local Government Act 2009.
classes.disposition_reason: No official record of these selections is published online; the Department of Local Governance site (dlg.gov.bt) does not answer from here.
